transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I hope it's okay to start with this, it's probably not a huge deal compared to what you usually see. But the main thing that pushed me to come in is... well, I've been having a little trouble at work. 

I process insurance claims, and lately I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Like, even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I find myself leaving my desk. It's not that I'm trying to slack off or anything, I promise! I just get a bit restless and need to stretch, I guess. But I really want to do a good job, so I figured I should ask a professional about it before it becomes an issue. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help with?

Can you tell me whether this restlessness and trouble staying at your desk is something you've noticed since you were a kid, or is it something that's really only started more recently, like in the past few months?

Um... well, to be completely honest, I guess it's not entirely new? Like, I really don't want to make it sound like I was a bad student or a troublemaker or anything, because I always tried my best to be good! But... looking back, I suppose I had some similar moments when I was younger. 

In elementary school, my teachers would usually tell my parents that I was a bright kid—which was really nice of them to say!—but they'd also write on my report cards that I, um, misplaced my worksheets a lot. Or they'd say I missed instructions and needed a few extra reminders to actually finish my classwork. It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult or ignore them, I just... kind of lost track of things sometimes, I guess. 

Does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers, or having trouble waiting your turn in lines or discussions?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I really try my best to be polite and listen when other people are talking. I'd hate to be rude or make anyone feel like what they're saying isn't important. 

I mean, maybe once in a great while I might get a little excited and speak up, but... no, I definitely don't blurt things out or cut in line or anything like that. I'm usually pretty quiet in discussions, actually. I hope that's a good thing? I just try to be respectful of everyone else's turn.
Do you notice similar issues with losing track of things, forgetting tasks, or getting easily distracted in other areas of your life, like at home or when managing personal responsibilities?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes? I really hate to admit it because I try so hard to stay on top of everything, but... yeah, I suppose it happens a bit more than I'd like. 

Like at work, sometimes I'll realize I forgot to do something simple, like returning a claimant's call right away, or updating a diary note in the system. Or, um, occasionally I might forget to send a form that I fully intended to send earlier in the day. It's never anything malicious, I promise! I just... I get sidetracked, I think. I really hope my supervisor knows I'm not doing it on purpose. 

At home, it's kind of similar, just little things slipping my mind. Is that normal? I mean, everyone forgets things sometimes, right? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it is.
Would you say these lapses in attention and restlessness have caused noticeable problems for you, like affecting your job performance, relationships, or daily responsibilities?

Um... well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has been a little bit of an issue at work lately. I really, really don't want to sound like I'm not doing my job, because I care a lot about my work and I always try to do the right thing! But, um... my supervisor recently had to put me on, well, they call it performance coaching. 

It's just because some of my claim files have been falling a little behind, and there were a few questions about my accuracy on some of the processing details. I know they're just trying to help me improve, which I really appreciate! But... it does make me a little worried. I was really hoping to get on the senior adjuster track soon, and I just... I'd hate for this to ruin my chances. I'm trying my best to fix it, I promise. Do you think this is something I can get better at? I really want to do a good job.

Looking back over the years since elementary school, would you say you've had these same struggles with distractibility, disorganization, and restlessness fairly consistently the whole time, or were there stretches—like in high school or early adulthood—where they went away and you felt fine?

Um... well, if I really think about it... I guess it's not exactly a new thing for me. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I was always very well-behaved, I promise. But, um... yeah, I suppose even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright, which is nice, right? But they'd also say things like... I lost my worksheets sometimes, or I'd miss parts of the instructions. 

They always said I just needed a few extra reminders to finish my classwork. I think I just got a little caught up in my own head sometimes. It never really went away completely in high school or when I started college, either. I just kind of... learned to try and work around it, I guess? I really hope that doesn't make me sound careless. I've always tried my absolute hardest to do what I'm supposed to do. Is it okay that I've always been a little like this?
Have you been experiencing any ongoing feelings of anxiety, low mood, or sleep problems recently, or do you use caffeine, alcohol, or other substances regularly?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I feel pretty okay most of the time! I'm not really an anxious person or anything, and my mood is usually pretty good, I think. I definitely try to keep a positive attitude! 

Sleep is... well, it's fine. I try to get a good amount of rest so I can be ready for work. And as for caffeine or alcohol... I might have a cup of coffee in the morning just to get going, like most people, but nothing crazy! And I don't really drink much alcohol or use anything else. I really try to take good care of myself. Is that what you were looking for? I hope that's a good answer.
Aside from getting up from your desk, do you often feel physically restless, fidget with your hands or feet, or have trouble sitting still even when you're expected to stay seated?

Um... well... I guess I do move around a little bit? I mean, I really try my best to sit still and look professional, especially when we have those longer team meetings or trainings. I know it's important to show respect to whoever is speaking! 

But, um... sometimes I don't even realize I'm doing it. Like, I might be bouncing my leg a little under the table, or... or clicking my pen. Sometimes I just find myself shifting around in my chair a lot, even when I'm really trying hard to look focused and pay attention. I try to keep it quiet so I don't bother anyone else, I promise! It's just... a little hard to stay perfectly still for that long. Is that... is that normal? I hope it doesn't make me seem like I'm not paying attention, because I really am trying to.
Do you often have trouble keeping your workspace, paperwork, or personal belongings organized, or find yourself frequently losing things like keys, documents, or your phone?

Um... well... I guess I wouldn't say I'm completely disorganized or anything like that. I really do try to keep things neat! But, um... recently, they gave me a bigger caseload at work, which is great, you know? It means they trust me! 

But, uh, since that happened... I guess my claim folders and my sticky notes and... well, all my email flags kind of end up all over the place. It's just a lot to keep track of all at once. And sometimes, when I look at it all, I just... I have a really hard time figuring out which policy review I should even tackle first. I really want to do a good job and stay on top of everything, but it just gets a little overwhelming sometimes. I usually find everything eventually, though! I hope that doesn't make me sound like a messy employee. I really do try my best to keep it all together. Is it okay that I struggle with that a little bit?

This continues to support a diagnosis of ADHD (F90.0) with mixed inattentive and mild hyperactive features rather than a purely inattentive-only presentation or a hyperactive-impulsive predominant type.

opening_question.intent: Establish the primary reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a childhood-onset (elementary school) pattern of inattentiveness—losing worksheets, missing instructions, needing reminders—that has persisted into adulthood, now manifesting as disorganization, forgetfulness, distractibility, and mild restlessness (leg bouncing, pen clicking, needing to get up) affecting occupational functioning (performance coaching at work). Hyperactive-impulsive symptoms are present but subthreshold (no interrupting, blurting, or significant impulsivity), while inattentive symptoms are pervasive across settings (work and home) and clearly impair functioning. No evidence of mood, anxiety, or substance-related etiology to better explain symptoms. This pattern most closely fits ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, though mild hyperactive features are also endorsed, warranting consideration of combined presentation as a differential.
